paragraphs.title: Opening: God’s Manifestation and Victory over the Wicked

easy.explanation: The psalm calls for God’s enemies to be scattered and those who hate Him to flee.
easy.q: What are God’s enemies asked to do?

easy.explanation: The righteous are told to be glad and rejoice before God.
The verse calls God a father of the fatherless.
easy.q: What is God called in relation to the fatherless?

answers: The destruction of the wicked before God
medium.explanation: Both images portray the wicked perishing in God’s presence.
medium.q: What do the images of disappearing smoke and melting wax emphasize?

answers: He sets the solitary in families and brings out prisoners
He leaves them in the wilderness
medium.explanation: God gives the solitary families and releases those bound with chains.
medium.q: What does God do for the solitary and those bound with chains?

medium.explanation: The people are told to sing praises, extol God, and rejoice before Him.
medium.q: What does the command “Sing unto God” require?

answers: The wicked perish while the righteous rejoice
The mountains rise while the seas fall
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the destruction of the wicked with the joy of the righteous.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in this opening section?

challenge.explanation: These titles emphasize God’s care and justice for vulnerable people.
challenge.q: What do the titles “father of the fatherless” and “judge of the widows” reveal about God?

answers: Praise responds to His power, protection, and salvation
Praise is unrelated to the passage
challenge.explanation: The call to praise follows descriptions of God’s victory, care, and deliverance.
challenge.q: Why is praise connected with the description of God’s actions?

paragraphs.title: Revelation in the Wilderness and Blessing of the Land

easy.explanation: The verse describes God going before His people through the wilderness.
easy.q: Where did God lead His people?
What happened to the earth in God’s presence?

easy.explanation: God sent a plentiful rain to confirm His inheritance.
easy.q: What did God send upon the land?

answers: The power and awe of God’s revelation
The peacefulness of a quiet village
medium.explanation: The earth and Sinai move at the presence of the powerful God of Israel.
medium.q: What does the shaking at Sinai communicate?

medium.explanation: The rain confirmed God’s inheritance when it was weary.
medium.q: What effect did the rain have on the inheritance?

medium.explanation: The word refers to the wilderness through which God led His people.
medium.q: What does “wilderness” mean in this context?

answers: God leads His people, reveals Himself at Sinai, and sends rain
God builds a palace, crowns a king, and starts a trade
God sends an army, loses a battle, and leaves the land
challenge.explanation: The verses move from wilderness guidance to Sinai’s revelation and then to rain.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes these verses?

answers: God both reveals His power and gives sustaining blessing
God is absent from the land
Rain has no connection with God
challenge.explanation: The passage joins divine awe with God’s life-giving provision.
challenge.q: What does the movement from trembling earth to plentiful rain suggest?

challenge.explanation: The congregation dwells in the land, and God prepares goodness for the poor.
challenge.q: For whom does God prepare goodness at the end of the section?

paragraphs.title: Victory, Rest, and the Beauty of Israel

answers: The woman at home divides the spoil
easy.explanation: The verse says that she who tarried at home divided the spoil.
easy.q: What happens after the kings of armies flee?

easy.explanation: Israel is compared to the wings and feathers of a dove.
easy.q: What bird is used in the comparison of beauty?

answers: The hill where God desires to dwell
easy.explanation: God desires to dwell on this hill forever.
easy.q: What does the hill of God represent?

answers: The rapid flight of enemy kings
medium.explanation: The phrase describes enemy armies fleeing quickly.
medium.q: What does “Kings of armies did flee apace” describe?

answers: The enemies flee while Israel is pictured with beauty and peace
Both groups are described as defeated
Israel flees while the kings rest
medium.explanation: The passage moves from military defeat to a peaceful, beautiful image of Israel.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the fleeing kings and the dove imagery?

medium.explanation: Bashan is used as an image of a high and notable mountain.
medium.q: What is meant by “the hill of Bashan” in the comparison?

challenge.explanation: The precious metals present Israel as beautiful and honored.
challenge.q: What does the dove covered with silver and gold suggest?

answers: To emphasize that God chose His own dwelling hill
To announce that all mountains disappeared
To show that God rejected the chosen hill
challenge.explanation: The question highlights God’s choice of the hill where He will dwell.
challenge.q: Why does the psalm ask, “Why leap ye, ye high hills?”

answers: They show His heavenly power and royal majesty
They show that He is alone and powerless
They describe an ordinary human procession
challenge.explanation: The multitude of divine chariots and angels emphasizes God’s greatness.
challenge.q: How do the chariots and angels strengthen the portrayal of God?

easy.explanation: The Lord is blessed because He daily loads His people with benefits and is their God of salvation.
easy.q: For what is the Lord blessed day by day?

easy.explanation: The psalm says that God shall wound the head of His enemies.
easy.q: What will God do to the head of His enemies?

answers: Bashan and the depths of the sea
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will bring His people again from Bashan and the depths of the sea.
easy.q: From which places does the Lord bring His people again?

medium.explanation: God saves His people and defeats His enemies.
medium.q: What two roles are joined in this section?

answers: To show complete deliverance from distant or overwhelming places
medium.explanation: The imagery presents God as able to rescue His people from anywhere.
medium.q: What is the purpose of bringing the people from Bashan and the sea depths?

answers: Deliverance from the power of death
medium.explanation: The phrase declares that deliverance from death belongs to God.
medium.q: What does “the issues from death” suggest?

answers: God’s continual care includes protection and victory over enemies
challenge.explanation: The passage joins daily blessing with God’s power to defeat hostile forces.
challenge.q: How does daily salvation relate to the warrior imagery?

answers: The thorough defeat of persistent enemies
challenge.explanation: The imagery emphasizes judgment on enemies who continue in sin.
challenge.q: What does the wound to the head and hairy scalp emphasize?

answers: After describing victory, the psalm shows God’s royal march in the sanctuary
It changes from victory to farming
It ends before any procession is mentioned
challenge.explanation: The victory leads into the sight of God’s goings as King in the sanctuary.
challenge.q: How does verse 24 connect with the following procession?

paragraphs.title: The King’s Procession and the Gathering of Israel’s Tribes

answers: By singers, players on instruments, and women with timbrels
easy.explanation: The procession includes singers, instrumental players, and damsels with timbrels.
These four tribes are specifically named in the passage.
easy.q: Which tribes are named in the procession?

answers: He commands Israel’s strength and is asked to strengthen His work
He removes all strength from the people
easy.explanation: The people acknowledge God as the source of their strength.
easy.q: What does God command concerning strength?

answers: Singers first, instrumental players after them, and women with timbrels among them
Women first, singers last, and no instruments
medium.explanation: The verse gives this order for the procession.
medium.q: What is the order of the musical participants?

answers: Unity and broad participation among Israel
The division of Israel into enemies
The departure of the tribes from the land
medium.explanation: Different tribes appear together in worship before God.
medium.q: What does the gathering of several tribes communicate?

answers: The source or community of Israel
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the people and source of Israel.
medium.q: What does “the fountain of Israel” most likely indicate?

answers: The holy King goes forth while the people honor Him with music
The King appears without any people
challenge.explanation: Royal movement is accompanied by organized praise and celebration.
challenge.q: How does the procession combine worship and kingship?

answers: God’s power is connected with His sanctuary and His work for His people
The temple is presented as a place of weakness
The people are asked to leave Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The passage connects God’s commanded strength with His temple at Jerusalem.
challenge.q: Why are strength and the temple mentioned together?

answers: To show that worship involves a broad gathering of Israel
To describe the destruction of the tribes
To separate Israel from all worship
challenge.explanation: The named tribes represent the wider participation of Israel.
challenge.q: Why mention several tribes rather than one?

paragraphs.title: The Submission of Nations and Blessing for All Kingdoms

easy.explanation: God is asked to rebuke the warlike people and scatter them.
easy.q: What does the psalm ask God to do to those who delight in war?

easy.explanation: The kings are said to bring presents to God’s temple.
easy.q: What will kings bring to God?

easy.explanation: All kingdoms of the earth are called to sing to God.
easy.q: Who is called to sing praises to the Lord?

answers: Warlike peoples give way to kings bringing presents
medium.explanation: The passage moves from rebuking war to nations bringing gifts.
medium.q: What major change occurs in the opening verses of this section?

medium.explanation: The verse declares that God’s excellency is over Israel.
medium.q: Where is God’s excellency said to be?

answers: Foreign rulers will approach God and acknowledge Him
The princes will hide from God
medium.explanation: The image presents nations approaching and stretching out their hands to God.
medium.q: What does “princes shall come out of Egypt” suggest?

answers: It extends from Israel to all kingdoms and the heavens
It narrows from the nations to one person
It moves from the temple to warfare only
challenge.explanation: The conclusion calls all earthly kingdoms to praise the Lord and celebrates His heavenly strength.
challenge.q: How does the scope of praise expand in the closing verses?

answers: His powerful voice displays the strength that the nations are called to acknowledge
challenge.explanation: God’s mighty voice and strength together reveal His authority.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God’s mighty voice and His strength?

answers: The God of Israel gives strength and power to His people and is blessed
challenge.explanation: The psalm ends by blessing God as the giver of strength and power to His people.
challenge.q: What is the final idea of the psalm?
